title: Zero-storage constraint causality for allocation low-storage-factor collapse

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the minimal LP-causality control before observing the direct physical-versus-LP factor comparison.

model_change_from_20h3: remove LevelDemand node and its link
keep Basin, 32 m3/day source, root40 priority2, external20 priority3 and 7.9999146676 m3/day BMI infiltration
compare free Basin storage-change variable against a diagnostic hard storage_change=0 constraint

storage_free.rationale: With no storage-preservation demand, both managed demands can be served by drawing accepted Basin storage; the final low-storage objective can maximize alpha to one.

storage_fixed_zero.rationale: With zero storage change enforced, lexicographic root-demand maximization can retain 32 only by attenuating the 7.9999147 m3 negative forcing to zero through alpha.

hypotheses: Removing LevelDemand while leaving storage change free eliminates the alpha collapse: alpha becomes one and both UserDemands are fully allocated from source plus Basin storage draw.
Imposing only storage_change=0, still without LevelDemand, restores the alpha=0 and 32/0 allocation pattern.

Therefore the 20H3 factor collapse is not specific to LevelDemand bookkeeping; it is caused by lexicographic allocation under a storage-preservation requirement with alpha available as a forecast degree of freedom.
